artifact.title: Facet Next: from review canvas to decision workspace

nodes.title: North star
nodes.text: Facet should become a full decision workspace with presentation quality that exceeds Lavish and review functionality that goes materially further. The goal is not decorative HTML volume: it is modular creative composition, excellent interaction design, durable collaboration, and substantially lower Codex usage. The product promise is: turn compact agent intent into a premium adaptive workspace, guide people from evidence to decision, then return precise feedback as tiny semantic changes.

nodes.title: What the first comparison tells us
nodes.text: Lavish currently wins visual hierarchy and presentation. Facet already has the stronger structured review foundation. The next release must close the visual gap without weakening its durable feedback loop or compact protocol.

rows: Decision-first layouts with stronger hierarchy and breathing room
Multiple deterministic compositions chosen from semantic intent
Correct but visually weak outside Decide mode
Clear state, rationale, consequences, and confident primary action
Comments, modes, anchors, history, and revisions are strong
Prove full workflow savings directly against Lavish

nodes.title: Four product pillars
nodes.text: 1. Composed clarity: every artifact receives an intentional visual hierarchy rather than identical stacked sections. 2. Review intelligence: comments, evidence, revisions, and decisions remain connected through stable semantic identity. 3. Creative range: the renderer offers premium native compositions without asking the model to emit CSS or JavaScript. 4. Token discipline: agents express meaning and changes; the host owns layout, behavior, accessibility, and polish.

nodes.title: Pillar 1 — Visual Engine 2.0
nodes.text: Introduce deterministic layout recipes selected from artifact semantics: executive brief, option showdown, evidence board, implementation roadmap, incident room, code-review cockpit, and metric dashboard. Add summary bands, weighted scorecards, side-by-side option cards, evidence/risk clusters, sticky decision summaries, and progressive disclosure. Preserve quiet chrome, one icon family, accessible contrast, 44-pixel touch targets, responsive reading widths, and reduced-motion support. The model chooses intent and emphasis; the renderer chooses responsive layout details. Use the shadcn reference as a compositional benchmark: quiet neutral foundations, crisp typography, deliberate borders, confident control states, and modular blocks. Facet must exceed it through task-aware composition and integrated review intelligence rather than ornamental effects.

nodes.title: Design reference — shadcn principles, Facet identity
nodes.text: Use shadcn/ui as a quality reference for composable accessible primitives, thoughtful defaults, calm neutral surfaces, disciplined spacing, clear component states, responsive sidebars, dialogs, sheets, tables, charts, and command interfaces. Do not clone its site or make shadcn a runtime requirement. Facet should translate those principles into dependency-light semantic renderer primitives and retain its own violet-and-cyan identity, review modes, local-first security boundary, and artifact protocol.

nodes.title: Color direction — neutral precision with expressive signals
nodes.text: Adopt a shadcn-inspired neutral foundation so content, evidence, and decisions carry the visual weight. Keep color purposeful: violet for primary action and active review state, cyan for keyboard focus and live location, and semantic colors for outcomes. These are proposed tokens and must pass automated and manual contrast checks before implementation.

rows: Primary actions, selected anchors, Decide mode
Outcome states reinforced by icon and text

nodes.title: Modular composition system
nodes.text: Build the UI as replaceable layers. Primitives guarantee accessibility and states; semantic blocks express review meaning; layout recipes compose blocks for a task; visual lenses let the user change perspective without regenerating content. Each layer remains deterministic and locally rendered so visual richness costs almost no additional model output.

nodes.title: Pillar 2 — Review superpowers
nodes.text: Add threaded anchored comments, visible annotation pins, reviewer status, a change map, side-by-side semantic revisions, unresolved-feedback filters, decision rationale, confidence, owner, due date, and superseded-decision history. Create a guided review flow: understand the brief, inspect evidence, compare options, resolve concerns, then decide. Keep Explore, Review, and Decide modes, but make their purpose immediately legible and preserve reading position between modes.

nodes.title: Pillar 3 — Native creative blocks
nodes.text: Expand the renderer with high-value semantic primitives rather than arbitrary markup: option cards, score matrix, evidence card, quote, key takeaway, assumption, constraint, recommendation banner, decision summary, before/after view, milestone lane, dependency map, and annotated media. Each block must define compact data, loading and error states, keyboard behavior, mobile composition, print/export output, and a readable fallback for older viewers.

nodes.title: Functionality beyond Lavish
nodes.text: Facet should pair premium composition with capabilities that improve the complete decision lifecycle. The differentiator is not the number of components; it is how evidence, discussion, change, and commitment remain connected.

rows: The same content becomes the right review experience for its purpose
Intent token selects reusable local composition
Switch among summary, evidence, risk, change, and decision views
No content regeneration or duplicated artifact
Understand exactly what changed and why
Stable IDs and compact revision history
Preserve choice, rationale, confidence, owner, and supersession
Trace recommendations back to assumptions, citations, risks, and comments
Review becomes explainable rather than merely attractive
Know what must be read or resolved before deciding
Completeness and unresolved concerns are visible
Requested changes update only affected content
Lower latency, context use, and revision tokens
Private work without an account, plus durable export
No hosted service required for the core workflow

nodes.title: Creative interaction ideas
nodes.text: Add a Decision Cockpit that condenses recommendation, unresolved risks, confidence, and next action into one focused surface. Introduce Evidence Gravity so strongly supported claims visually gain weight while uncertain assumptions remain visibly provisional. Offer Story mode for guided presentation, Board mode for spatial comparison, and Focus mode for deep reading from the same artifact. Add a Revision Radar that highlights semantic change by importance, a Devil's Advocate lens that foregrounds counterarguments already present in the artifact, and a Token Receipt that shows the cost of initial creation and each revision. These experiences must be derived from structured data—not generated decoration—and must remain readable without animation or color.

nodes.title: Pillar 4 — Token intelligence
nodes.text: Build an artifact compiler so the skill can send a short intent-oriented source format instead of hand-authoring full tuple structures. Apply schema defaults, reusable vocabulary, deterministic IDs, template references, and validation locally. Add a token-budget mode that selects the smallest lossless representation. Continue using compact patches for revisions and return a concise feedback digest so the agent reads only open comments and affected nodes. Report initial, revision, and cumulative workflow tokens separately; never hide retries or skill-loading cost.

nodes.title: Target architecture
nodes.text: The model communicates intent and evidence; deterministic local systems provide visual quality and interaction. This keeps creative richness in reusable code instead of repeatedly spending model tokens on presentation markup.

nodes.title: Implementation roadmap
nodes.text: Implement Facet sequentially through seven gated phases. Each phase must leave the repository buildable, preserve existing review behavior, and produce reviewable evidence. Estimates are working ranges for focused implementation, not calendar commitments. Publishing and hosted collaboration remain outside this plan until the local product passes Phase 6.

items: Phase 0 — Baseline and contracts (2–3 focused days): freeze competitive prompts, scoring rules, screenshots, current performance, token estimates, compatibility fixtures, and regression tests.

Phase 1 — Design foundation and shell (4–6 focused days): implement the neutral-plus-violet tokens, typography, spacing, accessible primitives, responsive application shell, navigation, review rail, command surface, and complete interaction states.

Phase 2 — Option Showdown vertical slice (5–7 focused days): build the adaptive recipe engine and redesign comparison, risk, recommendation, evidence, and decision blocks around one excellent end-to-end expense-tracker review.

Phase 3 — Review intelligence (6–8 focused days): add visible anchors, threaded feedback, review filters, guided progression, semantic change map, decision rationale, confidence, ownership, and supersession history.

Phase 4 — Token compiler and patch loop (5–7 focused days): compile compact intent locally, apply defaults and stable IDs, validate automatically, emit feedback digests, optimize patches, and display honest Token Receipts.

Phase 5 — Creative workspace modes (6–10 focused days): add Summary, Evidence, Risk, Change, Decision, Story, Board, and Focus lenses plus Decision Cockpit, Evidence Gravity, Revision Radar, and graceful legacy fallbacks.

Phase 6 — Competitive proof and release decision (7–10 focused days plus participant scheduling): run blind Facet-versus-Lavish comparisons, usability sessions, accessibility and performance audits, fix critical gaps, and decide whether a local alpha is ready.
data.summary: Proof, compose, deepen review, compile compactly, expand selectively, validate with people

nodes.title: Phase-by-phase delivery contract
nodes.text: Every phase has one dominant outcome and a measurable exit gate. Work that belongs to a later phase is recorded but not pulled forward unless it blocks the current gate.

rows: Reproducible current Facet/Lavish evidence pack and frozen contracts
Identical prompts, parity rubric, raw outputs, screenshots, and current test suite recorded
Production-quality modular shell and design primitives
375/768/1024/1440 layouts pass; keyboard, contrast, reduced motion, and all state variants pass
Option Showdown recipe with premium comparison and decision experience
Equal-content prototype is materially clearer than current Facet and wins internal side-by-side review
End-to-end evidence, comments, changes, and decision workflow
Feedback survives two revisions; unresolved work is visible; all flows work by keyboard and after restart
Intent compiler, digest, optimized patching, and Token Receipt
No fidelity loss; median patch remains at or below 15%; full workflow accounting includes prompts and retries
Multiple lenses and workspace compositions from one artifact
Switching modes requires no regeneration; legacy artifacts remain readable; interaction p95 stays below target
Competitive and human-validation report with release recommendation
At least 60% blind preference, 90% task completion, 40% workflow-token advantage, and zero critical accessibility failures

nodes.title: Rules for phase-wise implementation
nodes.text: These rules keep quality high and make rollback straightforward while the renderer, protocol, and skill evolve together.

items: Create a scoped implementation brief and acceptance checklist before each phase begins.
Keep every commit buildable and preserve unrelated user changes.
Add tests with each new primitive, block, recipe, state, and protocol behavior.
Compare desktop, tablet, and mobile screenshots before closing visual work.
Run keyboard, screen-reader semantics, contrast, reduced-motion, offline, restart, and export checks at the relevant gate.
Record token, bundle, latency, and compatibility changes without overwriting earlier evidence.
Do not add a new semantic block when an existing block plus a layout recipe can express the same meaning.
Do not move to the next phase with unresolved critical or high-severity defects.
Review and approve the phase result in Facet before beginning the next phase.
Keep publishing, marketplace release, accounts, and hosted collaboration out of scope until separately approved.

nodes.title: First proof sprint
nodes.text: Begin with Phase 0, then proceed to Phase 1 only after the baseline evidence and contracts are frozen. The first visible milestone is the redesigned Option Showdown vertical slice in Phase 2; the foundation phases exist to make that result reusable rather than a one-off mockup.

items: Phase 0.1 — Freeze five identical competitor prompts and the equal-content, equal-function scoring rubric.
Phase 0.2 — Capture untouched current outputs, screenshots, timings, failures, retries, and token estimates.
Phase 0.3 — Record current build, test, accessibility, responsive, offline, export, and patch baselines.
Phase 0.4 — Freeze compatibility fixtures and define which existing behaviors cannot regress.
Phase 0 gate — Review the evidence pack and approve the exact Phase 1 scope.
Phase 1.1 — Implement tokens and primitive states without changing artifact semantics.
Phase 1.2 — Build the responsive shell, collapsible navigation, review rail, command surface, and mode indicators.
Phase 1 gate — Complete visual, responsive, accessibility, performance, and regression review before Phase 2.

nodes.title: Definition of ‘better than Lavish’
nodes.text: Facet should make the claim only when quality and efficiency pass together. A visually attractive result that loses review capability or comparable content does not pass.

rows: At least 60% prefer Facet across comparable tasks
At least 90% complete comment and decision flows without assistance
At least 40% lower measured or clearly labeled estimated workflow tokens
Median patch at or below 15% of the full artifact
Zero critical violations; complete keyboard path
Ordinary local interactions below 100 ms p95
No missing claims, evidence, controls, or decision options

nodes.title: Risks to control
nodes.text: The largest risks are copying surface aesthetics without a distinct product thesis, growing a schema too large for agents to use efficiently, optimizing token counts by dropping content, and creating layouts that look impressive only for curated examples. Backward compatibility and readable fallbacks must remain mandatory as creative blocks expand.

data.mitigation: Gate every new block and recipe on repeated workflow value, parity tests, compact encoding, responsive and accessibility QA, and graceful rendering in older viewers.

nodes.title: Approve the next direction
nodes.text: Choose whether to start Phase 0 baseline work now or revise the phase boundaries before any implementation begins. Approval authorizes only Phase 0; later phases remain independently gated.

Phase 4 — Token compiler and patch loop (5–7 focused days): compile compact intent locally, apply defaults and stable IDs, validate automatically, emit feedback digests, optimize patches, and display honest Token Receipts.

Phase 5 — Creative workspace modes (6–10 focused days): add Summary, Evidence, Risk, Change, Decision, Story, Board, and Focus lenses plus Decision Cockpit, Evidence Gravity, Revision Radar, and graceful legacy fallbacks.

Phase 6 — Competitive proof and release decision (7–10 focused days plus participant scheduling): run blind Facet-versus-Lavish comparisons, usability sessions, accessibility and performance audits, fix critical gaps, and decide whether a local alpha is ready.

node.title: Rules for phase-wise implementation
node.text: These rules keep quality high and make rollback straightforward while the renderer, protocol, and skill evolve together.

items: Create a scoped implementation brief and acceptance checklist before each phase begins.
Keep every commit buildable and preserve unrelated user changes.
Add tests with each new primitive, block, recipe, state, and protocol behavior.
Compare desktop, tablet, and mobile screenshots before closing visual work.
Run keyboard, screen-reader semantics, contrast, reduced-motion, offline, restart, and export checks at the relevant gate.
Record token, bundle, latency, and compatibility changes without overwriting earlier evidence.
Do not add a new semantic block when an existing block plus a layout recipe can express the same meaning.
Do not move to the next phase with unresolved critical or high-severity defects.
Review and approve the phase result in Facet before beginning the next phase.
Keep publishing, marketplace release, accounts, and hosted collaboration out of scope until separately approved.

operations.value: Begin with Phase 0, then proceed to Phase 1 only after the baseline evidence and contracts are frozen. The first visible milestone is the redesigned Option Showdown vertical slice in Phase 2; the foundation phases exist to make that result reusable rather than a one-off mockup.
